page: Google Cloud Platform x4-megamem-1920-metal is a bare-metal server engineered specifically for ultra-large, memory-intensive workloads. It features 1920 dedicated physical vCPUs based on x86_64 architecture and provides 32,768 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of approximately 17.07 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This system includes no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPUs or hardware accelerators. System persistence depends on external network storage solutions. Because it is delivered as a bare-metal environment, workloads run directly on the physical hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead, optimizing memory access and compute availability.

With its massive unified memory footprint, the server is designed for single-node workloads that cannot be partitioned across distributed clusters. It fits mission-critical enterprise platforms, such as hyper-scale SAP HANA deployments, massive in-memory databases, and high-throughput transactional analytics systems.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-megamem-1920-metal is an enterprise bare-metal server built for massive memory workloads. Operating on an x86_64 CPU architecture, it features 1920 dedicated vCPUs and 32,768 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core ratio of 17.07 GB per vCPU. The server is provisioned without local storage or GPU hardware, directing operations to network storage for data persistence. By eliminating hypervisor overhead through a bare-metal execution model, the system maximizes resource access across its vast pool of compute and memory. This hardware profile addresses enterprise architectures that cannot be partitioned across distributed nodes, making it suitable for ultra-large in-memory database platforms, SAP HANA deployments, real-time data warehousing, and high-capacity transactional processing systems.
